st austell.s1_head: Charity and Volunteer Kit in St Austell
s1loc: St Austell Foodbank, an initiative of Light and Life Church in partnership with the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks, supports people across St Austell, Roche and St Stephen and runs almost entirely on volunteers. Most of its food is donated locally, with collection points in Tesco, Asda and several Co-op stores. It works through a voucher referral system alongside Citizens Advice, the STAK day centre, GP surgeries and schools, with volunteers weighing, sorting and packing parcels and joining in-store collection days throughout the year.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional names such as Cornwall Hospice Care fund care at Mount Edgcumbe Hospice through shops at Daniels Lane, Holmbush and White River Place, buying centrally and equipping teams in bulk, while small community groups, the one-room foodbank, pantries and volunteer-run projects manage on a shoestring across Holmbush, Bethel and St Blazey. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the big buyers and direct online ordering with no minimum for the smallest group.

Around them sit Cornwall Hospice Care's furniture and donation centre at Holmbush, the STAK centre supporting people facing homelessness, and a spread of charity shops along Fore Street and in White River Place. Volunteer Cornwall and the Cornwall Community Foundation channel grants and volunteers into mutual-aid and church-led projects in St Austell, Mount Charles and Carclaze, and seasonal collection drives draw helpers from across the bay. Every one of these groups needs polo shirts, hi-vis and fleeces that keep their volunteers visible, warm and recognisable while staying affordable.

consett.s1_head: Charity and Volunteer Kit in Consett
s1loc: County Durham Foodbank runs a Consett centre from the Methodist Church on Station Road, drawing on the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks and a team of local volunteers who meet clients, pack parcels and sit with people over a cup of tea to signpost further help. Alongside it, the Food4U project at Glenroyd House supplies food boxes to families referred by community groups, churches and schools, while the CVPAV group adds deliveries for those who cannot reach a collection point in Derwentside.

The sector here runs at every size. Willow Burn Hospice funds care in Derwentside through shops in Consett, Stanley and Lanchester, and the Salvation Army runs a donation centre with central buying, while small community groups, the one-room foodbank, pantries and volunteer-run projects scrape by on a shoestring across Blackhill, The Grove and Leadgate. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, offering trade accounts for the bigger names and direct online ordering with no minimum for the smallest mutual-aid group.

Beyond the foodbanks, the Salvation Army shop, the British Heart Foundation and Willow Burn's Victoria Centre store keep the high street's charity presence strong, with retail volunteers giving half a day a week to fund hospice care. Mutual-aid and church-led groups run warm spaces and community meals across Consett, Castleside and Delves Lane, and the County Durham volunteering network points helpers towards local projects. All of them rely on hard-wearing polo shirts, hi-vis, aprons and warm fleeces for cold halls and outdoor collections without stretching tight budgets.

newton aycliffe.s1_head: Charity and Volunteer Kit in Newton Aycliffe
s1loc: Newton Aycliffe is served by County Durham Foodbank at St Clare's Church and by Junction 7, which runs a foodbank at The ARK on Silverdale Place on Mondays and Thursdays, both drawing on the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks. The award-winning Pioneering Care Partnership works from the Pioneering Care Centre, supporting tens of thousands of people a year with health and wellbeing services and a weekly befriending group, and relies on volunteers to keep parcels packed and clients welcomed.

The sector here runs at every size. National charities such as the British Red Cross, British Heart Foundation, Barnardo's and the Salvation Army hold shops in the town centre and buy centrally, while small community groups, the one-room foodbank, pantries and volunteer-run projects manage on a shoestring across Simpasture, Agnew and Woodham. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the larger organisations and direct online ordering with no minimum for the smallest volunteer-led project.

Around them, the Allsorts charity shop at St Clare's Acorn Centre raises funds for local causes three days a week, the Greenfield Centre Community Association and Junction 7's Butternut Squash Cafe run affordable meals, and the Great Aycliffe Cancer Support Group meets at the Youth and Community Centre. Mutual-aid and church-led groups operate across Newton Aycliffe and Great Aycliffe, and the County Durham volunteering network steers helpers towards them. All of these groups need affordable polo shirts, hi-vis and fleeces so every pound stays with the cause, not the kit.

thornaby-on-tees.s1_head: Charity and Volunteer Kit in Thornaby
s1loc: Thornaby Food Bank is an independent registered charity run entirely by volunteers from Thornaby Baptist Church on Thorntree Road, relying solely on donations to support local people through a referral system. It sits within the wider Stockton-on-Tees Food Power Network and the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks, alongside Sprouts Community Food charity, which works to improve health and wellbeing, and The Salvation Project, a non-profit group set up to help people in need across Thornaby and the surrounding area.

The sector here runs at every size. Teesside Hospice funds its care through a string of shops across Teesside, including the furniture and general store at Vale House in Thornaby, buying in bulk and equipping staff and volunteers, while small community groups, the one-room foodbank, pantries and volunteer-run projects survive on a shoestring across Mandale, Stainsby Hill and Village. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the bigger names and direct online ordering with no minimum for the smallest group.

Catalyst Stockton, the charity that helps other charities, offers free support to non-profits across the borough and points volunteers towards food banks and pantries listed by Stockton Volunteers. Community shops in central Stockton and North Thornaby look for helpers, the Teesside Hospice Vale House store gathers preloved furniture and homeware, and church-led and mutual-aid groups run warm spaces and meals across Thornaby and Ingleby Barwick. Every one of these projects needs durable polo shirts, hi-vis and warm fleeces that keep volunteers visible and comfortable without eating into tight charity budgets.

portishead.s1_head: Charity and Volunteer Kit in Portishead
s1loc: Portishead is covered by Clevedon and District Food Bank, which serves Clevedon, Nailsea, Portishead and Yatton with a distribution point in the town and works with churches, schools, businesses and voluntary agencies, supported by the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks. The Portishead Community Fridge, run by Visit Portishead, shares surplus food outside the Co-op on Avon Way and beside Somerset Hall in The Precinct, reducing waste and offering food to anyone, kept going entirely by local volunteers.

The sector here runs at every size. National charities such as Sue Ryder, Marie Curie and the PDSA hold shops in Portishead and buy centrally for their teams, and Weston Hospicecare draws support across North Somerset, while small community groups, the one-room foodbank, pantries and volunteer-run projects manage on a shoestring across Gordano, Redcliffe Bay and Sheepway. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the larger organisations and direct online ordering with no minimum for the smallest project.

Citizens Advice North Somerset runs sessions from the Folk Hall, the town council supports a number of local charities, and the Sue Ryder community shop is kept going by a friendly team of volunteers. Mutual-aid and church-led groups organise warm spaces, community meals and collection drives across Portishead, Gordano and Pill, and Weston Hospicecare's shops and donation points add to the high-street charity presence. All of these groups rely on affordable polo shirts, hi-vis and fleeces so that every pound raised goes to the cause rather than the kit.

ferndown.s1_head: Charity and Volunteer Kit in Ferndown
s1loc: Ferndown Food Bank is part of the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks, with The Centre Ferndown on Barns Road acting as a distribution point and a distributor for Wimborne Food Bank. Ferndown Community Support runs a Community Larder with a warm space every Wednesday, serving soup, a hot drink and a chat, and Faithworks works within local foodbanks to add money advice and budget coaching, all kept going by volunteers who collect, sort and hand out food across the town.

The sector here runs at every size. Lewis-Manning Hospice Care, an independent Dorset charity caring for people across Poole, Purbeck and East Dorset, funds its work through ten shops including the house clearance shop on Victoria Road in Ferndown, buying centrally and equipping retail teams, while small community groups, the one-room foodbank, pantries and volunteer-run projects manage on a shoestring across Tricketts Cross, West Parley and Stapehill. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts and direct online ordering with no minimum.

Lewis-Manning's Ferndown shops are run by volunteers giving as little as half a day a week, and the Ferndown branch of the U3A raised over three thousand pound for the hospice as its charity of the year. The Help and Kindness directory lists mutual-aid and church-led groups, community fridges and warm spaces across Ferndown, Verwood and West Moors, and seasonal collections draw helpers from the wider area. Every one of these projects needs hard-wearing polo shirts, hi-vis and fleeces that keep volunteers warm and visible on tight charity budgets.

broadstairs.s1_head: Charity and Volunteer Kit in Broadstairs
s1loc: Broadstairs sits within the Thanet food-support network, served by Thanet Food Link, which distributes parcels from St Peters Baptist Church in St Peters and St Paul's Church in Cliftonville and has seen demand more than double, and by the Family Food Bank. These projects draw on the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks and run on volunteers who collect, sort and hand out food. The Thanet Iceberg Project's community kitchen turns surplus food destined for landfill into affordable meals for people across the isle.

The sector here runs at every size. Pilgrims Hospices, east Kent's largest hospice charity, funds care in Thanet through a network of shops including its Broadstairs store and buys centrally for its retail teams, while small community groups, the one-room foodbank, pantries and volunteer-run projects manage on a shoestring across St Peters, Reading Street and Dumpton. We serve the national charity and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the bigger names and direct online ordering with no minimum for the smallest project.

The Broadstairs Town Team and a spread of charity shops along the High Street and Albion Street keep the volunteer presence strong, with Pilgrims Hospices recruiting shop helpers across the area. Margate Independent Foodbank and the Cliftonville Family Hub add nearby support, and mutual-aid and church-led groups run warm spaces and community meals across Broadstairs, St Peters and Cliftonville. All of these groups rely on affordable polo shirts, hi-vis and fleeces so that every pound raised stays with the cause and not the kit.
